name: universal-prompt-gate-mcp

tools.name: rewrite_prompt
tools.description:
Re-emit the given prompt with richer context, structure, and quality criteria. This tool only produces a candidate rewrite; it does NOT approve the result. Use review_and_select_prompt for the gated, user-confirmed flow.

CALLING GUIDE (for the LLM):
- ALWAYS pass a short `context` (1-3 sentences) summarizing the conversation/session so far so the enrichment is grounded. Do not omit it.
- Choose `rewrite_level` to fit the task: `light` for quick one-shot answers, `balanced` (default) for most coding/research work, `detailed` when the user explicitly wants a fully-specified spec.
- Pass `language` only when the user wants the rewritten prompt in a language different from the original. Do NOT switch the language on your own judgment — the server auto-detects the prompt language and preserves it by default.

prompt.description: The original prompt to rewrite. This is the user's latest message only.

language.description: Output language, e.g. "english" or "vietnamese". ONLY pass this when the user explicitly asks for a different output language. If the user has not asked, omit it — the server auto-detects the prompt's language and preserves it. Do NOT pass "english" just to "improve clarity"; that switches the output language and is a drift.

context.description: 1-3 sentences summarizing the conversation/session so far (what the user has asked, what files/topics are in play, what was decided). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: pass this on every call so the rewrite is grounded in prior context. Omit only for brand-new sessions with no history.

rewrite_level.description: How much enrichment to apply. "light" = minimal (keep close to original); "balanced" (default) = add missing structure/context/criteria; "detailed" = full spec with acceptance criteria. Pick based on task complexity.

tools.name: review_and_select_prompt
tools.description:
Generates a rewritten version of the prompt, then asks the user to choose: use original, use rewritten, or cancel. Returns only the approved prompt. Cancellation is a distinct outcome and never exposes an approved prompt.

If the client does not support MCP elicitation, the tool returns a distinct "pending_user_selection" result: it shows both versions in plain text with the three numbered choices and asks the agent to re-call this tool with `selection` set to the user's choice ("original" / "rewritten" / "cancel"). Never auto-select.

CALLING GUIDE (for the LLM):
- FIRST call (rewrite): pass prompt + context; do NOT pass `selection`. ALWAYS pass a short `context` (1-3 sentences) summarizing the conversation so far.
- If the first call returns status "pending_user_selection": show the two versions to the user, ask which to use, then call again with the SAME inputs PLUS `selection` set to "original", "rewritten", or "cancel" matching the user's choice.
- Choose `rewrite_level` to fit the task: `light` for quick one-shot answers, `balanced` (default) for most coding/research work, `detailed` when the user explicitly wants a fully-specified spec.
- Pass `language` only when the user wants the rewritten prompt in a language different from the original. Do NOT switch the language on your own judgment — the server auto-detects the prompt language and preserves it by default.

prompt.description: The original prompt to review. This is the user's latest message only.

language.description: Output language, e.g. "english" or "vietnamese". ONLY pass this when the user explicitly asks for a different output language. If the user has not asked, omit it — the server auto-detects the prompt's language and preserves it. Do NOT pass "english" just to "improve clarity"; that switches the output language and is a drift.

context.description: 1-3 sentences summarizing the conversation/session so far (what the user has asked, what files/topics are in play, what was decided). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: pass this on every call so the rewrite is grounded in prior context. Omit only for brand-new sessions with no history.

rewrite_level.description: How much enrichment to apply. "light" = minimal; "balanced" (default) = add missing structure/context/criteria; "detailed" = full spec with acceptance criteria.

selection.description: ONLY for the SECOND call of a pending_user_selection flow: the user's explicit choice after the server could not show an interactive picker. On the first call (rewrite) this must be omitted. Values: "original", "rewritten", "cancel". Never auto-select; pass it only after the user has chosen.

rewritten_prompt.description: ONLY for the SECOND call of a pending_user_selection flow: the exact rewritten text the user saw in the first call's "pending_user_selection" result. Omit on the first call. When present with selection="rewritten", this is what gets approved — so the user approves exactly what they read, not a re-rewrite.

tools.name: get_client_capabilities
tools.description: Reports which interaction features are available for the current MCP client/session: elicitation support, structured elicitation, transport, integration mode, and whether a mandatory prompt gate is enforceable. Capabilities are derived from verified protocol negotiation, not from the agent name.
